page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is a compute-skewed virtual machine instance configured with 16 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, the machine features 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation. Cache dimensions consist of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, though advanced vector formats such as AVX-512 and AMX are not supported. This configuration does not include local storage, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate mid-tier performance across multi-threaded operations, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded throughput. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves 2680.97 in single-core and 21496.93 in multi-core metrics, falling within the middle 50% category. Geekbench benchmarking highlights a lower single-core score of 858.0 alongside an average multi-core score of 5488.0, with solid parallel results in clang software compilation (9282.0) and ray tracing (10990.0). Text processing and single-threaded data compression workloads register in the bottom decile, indicating limited capability for single-thread bound serial tasks.

Memory throughput and operational tests display steady mid-tier capability, recording uncached read speeds of 71.67 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 35.27 GB/sec. Application testing shows 15.91 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 12.91 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Small 135M parameter LLM inference runs at 904.78 tokens per second during prompt ingestion and 209.07 tokens per second during generation.

Operating at an allocation ratio of 1.0 GB of memory per core, the machine provides efficient multi-core density for parallel compute tasks that do not require heavy per-thread RAM. It is suitable for CI/CD builds, static web delivery, batch computing, and horizontally distributed microservices, provided workloads do not rely on local disk I/O or advanced vector acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM on an Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture operating at 2.2 GHz. The instance offers a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with dedicated CPU allocation, but includes no local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place multi-threaded throughput, PassMark scores, and Redis key-value operations within the middle tier, though single-core performance and text compression metrics rank lower. With uncached read bandwidth reaching 71.67 GB/sec and static web serving throughput at 12.91 GB/sec, it provides a balanced, cost-effective resource footprint for CPU-parallelized services, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized backend workloads.
